title.zh: 规定依照条约义务或国际承诺在外国参加任何战役或行动的菲律宾武装部队预备役军官免于转回非现役身份
title.en: An Act Providing for Security From Reversion to Inactive Status of Reserve Officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines Who Have Served or Will Hereafter Serve in Any Campaign or Operation in a Foreign Country in Compliance With Our Treaty Obligations or International Commitments.
title.orig: An Act Providing for Security From Reversion to Inactive Status of Reserve Officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines Who Have Served or Will Hereafter Serve in Any Campaign or Operation in a Foreign Country in Compliance With Our Treaty Obligations or International Commitments.

source.name: LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation）

completenessNote: 全文，共 3 条；逐字取自 LawPhil 菲律宾法律虚拟图书馆（The LawPhil Project – Arellano Law Foundation） 官方页面（statutes/repacts/ra1972/ra_6441_1972.html），未改写、未摘译、未节选；原文语言：英语。 条文抬头依源文为 “Section N.” 等形式，本库统一规范为 “Section N.”；首行抬头与条内标题的分段依源文块级边界还原。

text.en: Title of this Act .—This Act shall be known as the "Security From Reversion Act".

Reserve Officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines in the active service who served or: will henceforth serve in any campaign or operation in a foreign country in compliance with law shall be secured from reversion to inactive status, except upon their own request or for cause as may be adjudged by a court martial or by appropriate administrative bodies existing by provision of law in the Armed Forces of the Philippines: Provided, That the service of such officer in the foreign country shall not be less than twelve months: Provided, further, That in the case of the Philcag ands Philcom volunteers the period shall not be less than six months: Provided, further, That should an officer be wounded in action or contracts any disease or ailment that requires his recall to the Philippines, the period shall continue to be counted until he shall have been pronounced cured: And Provided, finally , That such services were rendered honorably.

Effectivity .—This Act shall take effect immediately upon its approval.
Approved, June 17, 1972.
